key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/powerpacker.library:0:10C6
name: decode_packed_bit_value
description: Decodes one value from the packed bit stream held in the decompressor state. It counts bits in a mask, combines bits of a stored word into the result, writes that result through the output pointer, and calls two other library routines.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/powerpacker.library:0:10CC
name: fill_zeros_wrapping_buffer
description: Writes zero words into a buffer while counting down a length, and wraps back to the stored buffer start when a width counter runs out. It is PowerPacker library code that clears a window of output words.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/powerpacker.library:0:10FE
name: fill_zeros_and_copy_block
description: Clears a run of words in a wrapping buffer, then decodes a bit value and copies a block with the exec CopyMemQuick call when the output position passes the stored limit. It is PowerPacker library code.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/powerpacker.library:0:1186
name: record_word_offsets_in_tables
description: Walks a range of 16-bit words and looks up each word's stored previous position in a table. When that lookup is non-zero it writes the computed offset into two output tables at a wrapped index, then stores the current position back into the lookup table.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/powerpacker.library:0:1210
name: record_byte_offsets_in_tables
description: Walks a range of bytes, uses each byte as an index into a table of stored pointers, and computes the distance from the stored position. When the distance is valid it writes a wrapped offset into two output tables, then updates the table entry to the current byte position.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/powerpacker.library:0:126A
name: record_byte_offset_one_table
description: Walks a range of bytes, uses each byte as an index into a pointer table, and computes the distance to the previous occurrence. When the distance is valid it writes one wrapped offset into a single output table, then updates the table entry to the current position.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/powerpacker.library:0:12C0
name: dispatch_calls_by_run_length
description: Compares a length counter against four. For short counts it makes a single call, and for longer counts it makes one call and then repeats a second call (count minus four) divided by three times before a final call. It is PowerPacker library code for run handling.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/powerpacker.library:0:12E6
name: chain_two_library_calls
description: Calls two other library routines in sequence and returns. It has no data handling of its own and only sequences the two calls.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/powerpacker.library:0:12F8
name: pack_bits_into_words
description: Shifts bits one at a time from a source word into an accumulator, and stores the accumulator as a word whenever its top bit is set. It grows the output buffer through a memory call when the output pointer reaches the stored limit.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/powerpacker.library:0:1340
name: allocate_sized_block
description: Allocates memory through the library's allocator vector with four extra bytes, stores the requested size in the first longword, and returns a pointer just past that header.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/powerpacker.library:0:135C
name: free_memory_if_nonnull
description: If the pointer in the A1 register is not zero, it calls the library's free routine through a vector stored in the library base. If the pointer is zero it returns without any work.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:00FA
name: open_library_save_entry
description: Opens a library by name through the exec vector and keeps the returned base. It then copies the first bytes of the entry at a fixed offset from that base into a record, and notes whether the entry is an absolute jump or a short branch.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:011C
name: save_patched_entry_target
description: Calls a library routine, then reads the saved entry bytes from the record. If they are an absolute jump it stores the jump target, and if they are a short branch it stores the branch target computed from the displacement.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:0146
name: decode_marked_branch_target
description: Checks whether a saved entry stub begins with a particular marker byte and a branch-always opcode. When both match it computes the branch target from the displacement and stores it in the record, otherwise it calls a library routine and stops.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:015C
name: store_branch_stub_target
description: Stores the second byte of a stub into the record and, when the stub is a branch-always opcode, computes and stores the branch target. Otherwise it calls a library routine, then finishes with one more library call.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:01C4
name: restore_stub_after_countdown
description: Decrements a countdown in the record and, once it reaches zero with a flag bit set, checks whether the stub still jumps to one of two known routines. If so it writes back the saved bytes and calls three library routines to finish.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:01D2
name: return_zero_handler
description: Returns zero in the result register and does nothing else. The library data table refers to it as a handler entry.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:01D6
name: restore_stub_release_library
description: If the saved stub still jumps to one of two known routines, it writes back the saved bytes, then clears the cache, closes the library, frees the memory block and removes the library entry.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:0264
name: set_countdown_flag_bit
description: Sets bit three of a flag byte stored in the library record. The flag marks that the countdown in restore_stub_after_countdown is armed.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:026C
name: find_crm_library_base
description: Looks up a library base through the system and checks that memory at its entry contains the text CrM.library together with a register-save opcode. If the check matches it calls one follow-up routine and returns the base.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:0276
name: match_crm_library_signature
description: Looks up a library base through the system and checks the memory at the returned entry for the text CrM.library and a register-save opcode. When both match it calls one follow-up routine and returns the high half of the lookup result.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:02C6
name: decrement_countdown_clear_cache
description: Decrements a 16-bit countdown in the library record and calls a library routine to clear the processor cache. When the library version exceeds a threshold it calls a second library routine, then returns its first argument unchanged.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:02EC
name: advance_countdown_then_callback
description: Decrements a byte countdown in the record and returns early while it is not yet zero. At zero it calls a stored routine using an offset from the record, runs three library calls and a memory free, then clears a stored pointer word.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:0340
name: spin_delay_countdown
description: Counts a 16-bit value down from a register-held start to minus one in a loop that does nothing else. It acts as a short busy-wait.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:0358
name: copy_nonzero_count_blocks
description: Copies a table of 16-bit counts from the record into a reversed working area. For each non-zero count it copies that many longwords from the source to the destination through a helper, and a second loop does the same for a flagged path.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:03CA
name: decode_lz_copy_or_literals
description: Decodes one token from the bit stream: either a run of literal bytes produced by a helper, or a match whose length comes from a set of bit tests and whose distance comes from a masked table lookup. A match copies bytes backward from earlier output.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:03FA
name: decode_match_block_copy
description: Reads a length from bit-tested selectors and a distance from a masked table, then copies a block of earlier output forward to the current position. It loops until the output pointer reaches the stored limit.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:040A
name: decode_selected_match_copy
description: Chooses a length from a sequence of bit tests and adds a value from a lookup, then copies that many bytes backward within the output buffer. The loop repeats until the output pointer reaches the limit.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:0414
name: decode_literal_then_match
description: Writes literal bytes obtained from a helper when the bit test is clear, otherwise computes a length and copies backward from earlier output. It repeats while the length counter has not run out.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:041E
name: decode_match_small_selector
description: Selects a small base length from a short chain of bit tests, adds a decoded value, and copies that many bytes backward from earlier output. It stops when the output pointer reaches the stored limit.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:0428
name: decode_bitstream_match_table
description: Decodes a match from the bit stream by reading a masked table value, computes the source position from the output pointer, and copies the block backward. It repeats while the output has not reached the limit.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:0444
name: copy_long_run_from_stream
description: Decodes a run length from a bit-tested selector and writes that many bytes from a helper into the output buffer, moving backward. It ends when the output pointer reaches the stored limit.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:044E
name: copy_short_run_backwards
description: Uses a fixed base length when a flag bit is set, adds a decoded value, and copies that many bytes backward from the output pointer. It loops until the output reaches the limit.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:0466
name: select_halved_or_input_word
description: Returns the word in the D6 register shifted right by one when the counter in D7 equals one, otherwise returns the word passed in D0 unchanged. The decoder uses it to pick a scaled or raw value.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:04B2
name: return_without_action
description: Contains only a return, so it changes no memory or registers. One other routine refers to it.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:04B4
name: allocate_use_free_block
description: Allocates a memory block through the library's allocator vector. If the allocation succeeds it passes the block to one helper routine and then releases the block through the free vector.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:04EA
name: build_code_lookup_table
description: Clears a 16-entry counter table, reads code lengths from the bit stream and fills a 16-bit lookup table for each code. It repeats until a finishing flag is set.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:058E
name: decode_symbol_bit_by_bit
description: Reads bits one at a time from a bit buffer into an accumulated code, and stops as soon as the code is no larger than a limit from the decode table. It then returns the symbol stored at that table index.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:0598
name: decode_symbol_by_limits
description: Reads bits one at a time into an accumulator, testing it against the code limit for each length from 1 to 16. When the limit is met it returns the symbol stored at the corresponding table position.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:062A
name: fill_accumulated_code_tables
description: Sets the first table entry to zero, then runs fifteen steps that accumulate counts from a source array into running sums. It writes those sums into two tables at each index to prepare offsets for the symbol decoder.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:065E
name: return_empty_routine
description: Contains nothing but a return, so it changes no memory or registers. One other routine refers to it.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:0660
name: classify_crm_file_signature
description: Checks that the input pointer is word aligned, reads the first four bytes, and maps the tags CrM!, CrM2, Crm! and Crm2 to codes 1, 2, 16 and 17. Any other value gives zero.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:06A2
name: apply_delta_sum_when_flagged
description: If the input is word aligned and non-zero, it reads a count and a start value from the record. When a flag bit is set it turns the buffer into a running sum of its bytes, otherwise it only calls a helper.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:libs/CrM.library:0:06EE
name: accumulate_bytes_running_sum
description: Calls a stored routine, then adds each following byte onto the previous byte in place, repeating for a count held in D1. The result is a running sum over the buffer.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:cap.amg:0:0000
name: open_crm_library_retry
description: Program entry that repeatedly tries to open the CrM.library by name through the old open-library call until it gets a base. It then makes one more library call on that base.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:Wait:0:0000
name: find_max_then_fill_buffer
description: Walks a linked list of entries to find the largest value in a field, then allocates a buffer if the allocation succeeds. It writes the maximum as a leading word followed by a run of incrementing words, and calls a routine that prepares the buffer.

key: combat air patrol (1992)(psygnosis)[cr xpress]/Combat Air Patrol (1992)(Psygnosis)[cr Xpress].adf:Wait:0:0136
name: copy_sixteen_longs_then_call
description: If the destination pointer is not zero, it copies sixteen longwords from a fixed area into it. It then calls one library routine.

name: decode_block_into_low_memory
description: Zeroes low memory, then copies 3000 longwords from a source block into low memory, XORing each with a constant. It then writes a jump and a return instruction into fixed low-memory locations and touches the DMA and interrupt control registers.

name: set_low_bit_and_return
description: Sets bit zero of the low byte of D0 and returns that value. The reference run never reached it, and the decompiler only shows it as a gap in the code.

name: write_branch_instruction_word
description: Writes a branch-always instruction word to a fixed low-memory location and returns the low byte of D0 unchanged. One other routine reaches it through an address load.

name: call_stored_routine_passthrough
description: Calls a routine whose address is read from a fixed offset in the work area, then returns the two input registers unchanged.

name: reset_entries_when_negative
description: When a status value is negative, it clears the first word of thirty-one table entries that are 98 bytes apart. It then zeroes a status word, calls helpers, and sets an index and a counter before calling one more routine.

name: set_state_fields_from_lookup
description: When a mode value is not two, it resets a state byte and writes two fixed words, then looks up a value through two indexed tables and stores it if it is positive. When the mode is two it sets the state byte and, if a condition holds, stores two positions.

name: advance_state_timer_fields
description: Checks a state flag and a counter, and while the counter is still running it decrements it and returns. When the counter ends it resets it from a table value, adds a constant to a second value, and writes two fields, calling three helpers.

name: advance_state_machine_step
description: Runs one step of a small state machine: it moves from state zero to one and then to two when a flag and a level check pass, and resets to state zero otherwise. Each step writes a few fields in the entry and calls helpers.

name: check_slot_table_and_activate
description: When the status flags are clear it counts down a timer and reloads it from a table. If none of the thirty-one entries in a table is active, it sets an active flag, reads a value indexed by a counter, and calls helpers to fill in an entry.

name: set_bits_and_update_entry
description: Sets a fixed group of bits in a word at an offset from the input pointer. When the active flag is set it decrements a timer in the entry, checks a second flag, and updates the entry position through helper calls.

name: activate_entry_with_value
description: Marks the entry at the A0 pointer as active by setting one flag byte, stores the D0 word at a fixed offset, and sets a second flag byte to one. It returns at once.

name: enable_entry_clear_secondary
description: Sets a flag byte in the entry at the A0 pointer to one, stores the D0 word at a fixed offset, and clears a second flag byte to zero. Only these field writes are visible in the listing.

name: check_entry_proximity_match
description: When the first entry is in state two, it compares its horizontal position with a second entry's, shifted by a bit-dependent offset. A match needs an absolute horizontal difference under nine and a vertical difference under 17, after which it records the offsets, sets two size fields to nine and moves to state four.

name: init_state_lookup_from_table
description: When the state value is above three it resets several fields and searches a byte table for the current code. It then stores the matching word from a second table, choosing between two tables by a flag.

name: start_timed_state_transition
description: When a counter is zero, it checks a state value and an elapsed count against thresholds and then sets a status code. It calls a helper, reads a position from an indexed table, and keeps the second position field between 80 and 224.

name: advance_position_from_table
description: Returns the D0 word with bit zero set. When the active counter is non-zero it updates the entry position, and in state two it adds an increment from a table that steps and wraps back to the start at a fixed count.

name: set_mode_six_return_byte
description: Sets a mode byte to six and returns the low byte of D0 with every bit set except bit zero.

name: copy_table_entry_when_free
description: When a flag byte is clear, it reads a record from a table chosen by a counter. If the record's first word is no larger than the current value and its second word is zero, it starts a four-step timer and copies the record's third word into the state.

name: step_timer_and_mark_entry
description: While a timer is running it calls a helper, clears entry fields, marks a table slot as used, and increments a step counter that stops at 20. If the timer is not running it clears the entry once its position passes 191.

name: clear_linked_entry_fields
description: Walks ten tables of records, each ending at a sentinel word, and zeroes the second word of every record. It resets the record tables this way.

name: fill_free_slot_entry
description: After a short warm-up count, and when no other entries or flags are active, it checks a counter every eighth step. It then searches the entry table for a free slot and fills that slot's position fields from a lookup table.

name: expire_out_of_range_entries
description: Walks a short list of entries and clears those whose flag byte is negative and that meet a position range check. It calls helper routines for the other entries.

name: return_noop_entry
description: Contains only a return, so it changes no memory or registers. The reference run executes it.

name: return_noop_stub
description: Contains only a return, so it changes no memory or registers. The reference run enters it from outside the static flow.

name: write_new_entry_when_close
description: When a flag byte and two other flags are clear, it compares the entry's vertical position with a reference. A difference under nine horizontally and a second check under 97 must both pass, and then a counter-gated branch writes a new record with fixed field values and sets a timer.

name: return_immediately_stub
description: Contains only a return, so it changes no memory or registers. The reference run enters it from outside the static flow.

name: return_gap_stub
description: Its listing is a bare return. The fact sheet counts fourteen instructions, so the rest of the gap is not decoded here.

name: queue_entry_after_timer
description: When no blocking flags are set it counts a timer down and reloads it from a table. If a slot in a small table is free and the state allows, it writes a new entry with a fixed type value and positions taken from a table.

name: advance_entry_after_countdown
description: While an entry is active and not in a blocking state, it counts a timer down. When the timer expires it clears several entry fields, adds a constant to a counter, and updates the entry state.

name: step_script_table_state
description: Switches on a mode value: mode one clears an entry flag when a range check fails, and mode two clears an activity flag when a position passes a limit. Otherwise it steps through a table of values until a sentinel value is reached.

name: sort_entries_by_key_field
description: Clears a 1568-byte work block, then copies active entries from the table into it in order of a key byte, one slot at a time, and links them with sorted indices. It finally copies the work block back out.

name: copy_work_entries_back
description: Copies the work block of entry records back into the entry table, as the mirror of the copy done before sorting. It copies the full block in sequence.

name: call_then_return_stub
description: Calls one routine and returns. It contains no other work.

name: spawn_entries_by_type
description: In state two, when a table entry's position is at or below a computed limit, it advances the table cursor. If no blocking flags are set it switches on the entry's type byte, and each case fills free slots of the entry table with records from fixed tables.

name: fill_free_slots_with_records
description: Clears a counter and reads a value from a bit-selected table. It then fills up to ten free slots of the entry table with records that have fixed field values and a position taken from that value.

name: run_callbacks_for_active_entries
description: In state two it either advances a counter or clears a flag bit on free entries. It then calls a stored routine for each active entry in the table.

name: run_callbacks_second_table
description: In state two it calls a stored routine for each active entry of a second entry table, which starts at a different address from the first.

name: call_three_helpers_undecoded
description: The decompiler timed out, so only the listing facts are known: the routine has 39 instructions and calls three other routines. The reference run executes it, but its purpose cannot be stated from this evidence.

name: initialise_record_block_from_table
description: Sets flag and value fields in a block of nine records, writing a constant into a shared field and copying words from a source table into each record's position fields.

name: initialise_offset_record_block
description: Fills nine records with fixed field values and source-table words, the same as its neighbour, but starting at a different offset in the record area.

name: fill_records_from_pair_list
description: Walks a list of pointer pairs, writing position fields and fixed field values into consecutive records. It advances to the next pair until the count runs out.

name: set_high_bits_return_byte
description: Returns the low byte of D0 with every bit set except bit zero. One routine takes its address, and the reference run does not reach it directly.

name: run_entry_callbacks_then_routine
description: When a flag byte is set, it calls a stored routine for each active entry in the entry table. It then calls one more routine chosen from a small pointer table by a counter.

name: run_eight_helpers_then_clear
description: Calls eight other routines in sequence and then zeroes a state byte. It has no other logic.

name: step_position_counter_loop
description: Clears two state values, then loops over a step counter, calling helper routines and reading a value tied to the position counter. It selects table values by the counter's range and returns its result with bit zero set.

name: set_flag_run_six_helpers
description: Sets a flag byte to one, then calls six other routines in sequence and returns.

name: write_table_records_to_block
description: Sets a flag byte to one, then copies three words from each record of a selected table into a fixed block. It calls a helper after each record until the count ends.

name: run_helper_set_by_mode
description: Sets a flag byte to one and calls a set of helper routines. The number of calls depends on whether a global value equals five. The gap is decoded as code, so nothing further is claimed.

name: run_six_helper_calls
description: Calls six other routines in sequence and returns.

name: copy_fixed_block_forward
description: Copies a fixed block of 320 records of ten longwords each from one memory area to another, moving forward through the block.

name: clear_fixed_block_records
description: Zeroes the same 320-record block that its neighbour copies, writing ten longwords per record.

name: run_four_helper_calls
description: Calls four other routines in sequence and returns.

name: run_seven_helper_calls
description: Calls seven other routines in sequence and returns.

name: initialise_entry_parameters
description: Writes a fixed set of starting values into a parameter block: a mode value of two, several position words, and a table index. It returns with no other work.

name: copy_tile_list_to_buffer
description: Reads a list of tile indices until a terminating value. For each tile it copies eight rows of four bytes from that tile's data into the destination, writing alternate bytes for even or odd columns, and moves on four bytes per tile.

name: run_three_count_helper_loops
description: Calls one helper fifteen times in a loop, with a five-call loop before and after it. The three loops run in sequence.

name: run_five_helper_loops
description: Calls one helper in five successive loops of five, four, two, four and ten calls.

name: format_decimal_digits
description: Writes the decimal digits of the D0 value into a text buffer from the least significant digit upward, after placing a terminator byte at the end. The digit count comes from the D1 register.

name: count_down_skipping_odds
description: Steps a 16-bit counter down through its values, moving past odd values, until it wraps past zero. It writes no memory.

name: count_down_skipping_evens
description: Decrements a 16-bit counter repeatedly, moving past even values, until it wraps past zero. It writes no memory.

name: fill_buffer_with_dashes
description: Fills a twelve-byte buffer with the character code for a dash, and toggles the high bit of a status byte around a helper call.

name: read_table_byte_by_index
description: Returns the byte from a table at an index formed by doubling the low byte of D0, read through the work-area base.

name: call_helper_then_loop_eight
description: Calls one helper, then calls another helper eight times in a loop.

name: call_helper_after_eight_loop
description: Calls one helper, then calls another helper eight times in a loop. It is the same routine shape as its neighbour.

name: adjust_index_from_flag_bits
description: Waits until a counter reaches six, then adjusts an index from four flag bits of a status byte and masks it to five bits. It writes a dash into the buffer at that index and calls helpers.

name: advance_counter_with_wrap
description: Adds one to a byte counter that wraps at 256 and calls a helper, then increments a second counter. When the second counter passes 249 and a state equals six it sets a flag and copies a table word, otherwise it resets the second counter.

name: copy_table_block_into_record
description: Advances an offset, reads a byte index from a table, and copies a block of longwords from a lookup table at that index into the target record. It repeats for six iterations.

name: copy_backward_longword_blocks
description: Copies longwords from a fixed source area backward into the target, sixteen per iteration over five iterations. The source position comes from an offset read from a table.

name: write_blocks_after_status_waits
description: Waits on a status bit before each group of word writes to a fixed set of locations. It loops over a fifteen-step and an eight-row pattern, with values taken from a table.

name: write_rows_after_status_wait
description: Uses the same wait-then-write loop as its neighbour, waiting on a status bit before each group of writes to fixed locations.

name: program_blitter_row_copy
description: Waits on a status bit and programs the blitter modulo, pointer and size registers in a loop over rows, using the same wait-and-write pattern as its neighbours.

name: clear_strided_buffer_rows
description: Zeroes four groups of ten longwords per row across a buffer, with the row count taken from a status byte. It then programs the blitter registers.

name: disable_dma_and_interrupts
description: Writes a value with the top bit clear and all other bits set to two fixed DMA and interrupt control registers. With the top bit clear, the write disables the bits it names.

name: set_dma_and_interrupt_control
description: Writes three fixed words to the DMA control, interrupt request and interrupt enable registers. The last word has the top bit clear, so it clears every bit it names.

name: write_one_hardware_value
description: Writes one value to a fixed hardware address and returns. The listing shows only that write.

name: advance_counter_run_helpers
description: Increments a counter byte, calls five helper routines and one further routine in sequence, then writes a fixed value to a status location.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: The listing is only a decoder halt, so these bytes are not usable code here. It is reached through address-based bit operations, and its purpose cannot be stated from this evidence.

name: clear_fixed_byte_block
description: Ors a fixed bit pattern into the word at the input pointer, then zeroes a block of 4314 bytes starting at a fixed address. Several other routines have the same clearing loop, each for its own block.

name: clear_fixed_byte_block
description: Zeroes 4314 bytes at its own fixed start address, one byte at a time. Several other routines have the same listing, each clearing its own block.

name: clear_fixed_byte_block
description: Zeroes 4314 bytes at its own fixed start address, one byte at a time. Several other routines have the same listing, each clearing its own block.

name: clear_fixed_byte_block
description: Zeroes 4314 bytes at its own fixed start address, one byte at a time. Several other routines have the same listing, each clearing its own block.

name: clear_fixed_byte_block
description: Zeroes 4314 bytes at its own fixed start address, one byte at a time. The listing shows only this loop, although the fact sheet counts many more instructions.

name: clear_fixed_byte_block
description: Zeroes 4314 bytes at its own fixed start address, one byte at a time. The listing shows only this loop, although the fact sheet counts many more instructions.

name: clear_fixed_byte_block
description: Zeroes 4314 bytes at its own fixed start address, one byte at a time. The listing shows only this loop, although the fact sheet counts far more instructions.

name: clear_fixed_byte_block
description: Zeroes 4314 bytes at its own fixed start address, one byte at a time. The listing shows only this loop, although the fact sheet counts many more instructions.

name: clear_fixed_byte_block
description: Zeroes 4314 bytes at its own fixed start address, one byte at a time. The routine also makes one further call that the listing does not show.

name: wait_raster_then_set_bits
description: Waits until the raster position register reads a fixed value, then clears bit zero of one byte and sets the top bit of a control byte. The top-bit set is repeated four times.

name: spin_forever_loop
description: Loops forever without any work, so once entered it never returns. One other routine enters it.

name: wait_raster_then_toggle_bits
description: Waits until a counter reaches a reference value, then waits for the raster position register to read a fixed value. It toggles bit zero of one byte and the top bit of a control byte, repeating the top-bit toggle four times.

name: toggle_control_top_bits
description: Toggles bit zero of one byte and the top bit of a control byte, with the top-bit toggle repeated four times. It does not wait for anything.

name: halt_when_marker_set
description: When a status value equals the character c, it enters an endless loop. Otherwise it returns, so it acts as a fail-stop check.

name: set_display_control_registers
description: Writes a fixed sequence of words to the display registers: the bitplane modulos, the control registers, the data fetch start and stop, and the display window start and stop.

name: set_blitter_masks_and_control
description: Writes fixed words to the blitter first-word and last-word mask registers and to its control registers.

name: repeat_three_helper_calls
description: Repeats a group of three helper calls forty-four times, then returns.

name: compute_entry_draw_offset
description: When the status word equals one and the entry's position is inside the allowed range, it works out a horizontal clip and shift. It derives a destination offset from the entry's coordinates, then calls one helper to finish.

name: blit_masked_rows_status_two
description: For status two it computes clip and shift values like its neighbours, then combines shifted mask and source words into destination rows with bitwise AND and OR.

name: blit_masked_rows_alternate
description: Computes clip and shift values for an entry record and combines shifted mask and source words into the destination rows, the same blit pattern as its neighbours, read from different field offsets.

name: blit_masked_rows_status_three
description: For status three it computes clip and shift values and combines shifted 32-bit mask and source words into destination rows, inverting the mask.

name: call_helper_forty_four_times
description: Calls one helper forty-four times in a loop and returns.

name: clear_entry_plane_columns
description: When the status is one, it picks a plane base address and a column count from the entry. It then zeroes four longwords spaced across the plane area for each column.

name: clear_entry_plane_columns_alt
description: Zeroes the same four-plane column pattern as its neighbour, choosing the plane base and count from the entry by a parity bit, with no status check.

name: clear_high_plane_columns
description: Zeroes four-plane column groups from a fixed high plane base, with the count taken from one entry byte.

name: combine_plane_rows_inverted
description: Loops over 480 rows of sixteen words, ORs each group of four source words, inverts the result, and stores it in the destination words.

name: combine_plane_rows_or
description: Ors each group of four source words into a destination word without inverting, storing 32 words per pass. The loop runs until its 16-bit counter wraps.

name: copy_tile_bytes_to_planes
description: Reads a list of tile indices until a terminating value of all ones. For each tile it copies eight rows of four bytes into four bitplanes at fixed spacing, then moves one byte to the right.

name: composite_tile_words_into_planes
description: Reads a list of tile indices until a terminating value. For each tile it combines sixteen rows of four words with four bitplanes: each plane is masked with the inverted OR of the four source words and then ORed with its word.

name: return_stack_value_passthrough
description: Returns the value held on the stack without changing registers. It has no other work.

name: copy_tile_words_to_planes
description: Reads a list of tile indices until a terminating value. For each tile it copies sixteen rows of four words from the tile data into four bitplanes at fixed spacing, moving one word to the right after each tile.

name: clear_sixteen_word_rows
description: Zeroes 512 consecutive groups of sixteen words.

name: copy_sixteen_word_rows
description: Copies 512 consecutive groups of sixteen words from the source to the destination.

name: split_source_into_four_planes
description: Copies 800 groups of twenty source words into four destination planes, distributing five words to each plane per group at fixed spacing.

name: copy_and_run_patched_routine
description: Modifies a couple of bytes near base registers, copies sixteen words from the source into a fixed buffer, and calls that buffer. The patch looks like a self-modifying code step.

name: store_word_indexed_then_call
description: Stores the D0 word in a table at an offset set by D1 doubled, then calls another routine.

name: build_three_field_counts
description: Loops over seven rows of sixteen words. For each word it compares three three-bit fields against falling thresholds and adds one to a count word for each field that passes, calling a helper after each row.

name: reduce_three_field_values
description: Loops over seven rows of sixteen words and subtracts one from each non-zero three-bit field in every word. It calls a helper after each row.

name: clear_sixteen_words_call_helper
description: Zeroes sixteen words starting at a fixed pointer, then calls one helper.

name: load_palette_from_words
description: Writes sixteen words, each shifted left by one bit, into the colour registers starting at the first one, then returns.

name: enable_cia_interrupt_mask
description: Writes a fixed value to the first CIA interrupt control register, which enables the interrupt sources its bits name, then calls two other routines.

name: reset_state_on_code
description: Checks a state byte against two codes. One code clears two fields to zero, and the other sets a value to one and clears two fields. Otherwise it returns with no change.

name: pulse_status_byte
description: Writes two to a status byte and then zeroes it, leaving the byte cleared.

name: map_status_to_code_value
description: Turns a status byte into a small code value. Depending on the byte's range and parity, and on two neighbouring bytes, it stores one of 0, 1, 2, 4, 8 or 128, and it stores 0 when nothing matches.

name: return_bare_stub
description: Contains only a return, so it changes no memory or registers. It is called by one other routine.

name: advance_table_every_ten
description: When a flag is set it counts a byte up to ten. At ten it resets the count, flips the top bit of a status byte, and loads the low nibble from a table that it steps through, wrapping on an end marker.

name: rotate_status_write_serial
description: If bit three of a status byte is set, it rotates the byte, flips its sign bit and writes a fixed sequence of values to the CIA keyboard serial and timer registers. Otherwise it writes one fixed value and returns.

name: decode_joystick_direction_bits
description: Reads the joystick port movement registers and the fire-button register, then combines their bits into direction flags in a status word. It does nothing when a flag is set.

name: store_word_parts_status
description: Writes parts of a word to two status locations, then writes a fixed value to a third location.

name: store_word_parts_status
description: Writes parts of a word to two status locations, then writes a fixed value to a third location. It has the same listing as its neighbour.

name: read_mouse_button_deltas
description: Computes the negated change between the previous and current mouse movement values and stores both. It sets flag bits from the fire and right-button registers.

name: silence_audio_channels
description: Clears the four audio channel volume registers and writes a fixed value to the DMA control register, which silences the channels.

name: update_channel_bit_by_mode
description: For a record whose state is one, it sets, clears or rotates a bit in a status byte according to a mode field, then clears a counter. Otherwise it stores two parameters, calls helpers and marks the record active.

name: run_conditional_helper_calls
description: Calls a helper, then conditionally calls one or two more helpers depending on a flag and a state byte, and returns.

name: write_single_status_value
description: Writes one value to a fixed status location and returns.

name: write_status_value_then_return
description: Writes one value to a fixed status location and returns. The fact sheet also lists one routine call that the listing does not show.

name: poll_channel_interrupt_flags
description: Loops over ten channel records, testing one bit of the interrupt request word for each. When the bit is set and the record has a flag, it marks the record and sets its pointer and count from a linked source.

name: initialise_channel_records
description: Sets starting values in the channel records and points three fields at table entries chosen by a byte. It then fills two tables with ramps that step by fourteen up to 112 and writes terminator bytes.

name: step_event_stream_sequencer
description: When a playing flag is set it counts down a per-step timer and reads command bytes from an event stream. An end marker stops the stream, a code byte sets a duration, and other bytes write values into a table. It returns a status value.

name: set_byte_to_one
description: Writes one to the byte at the input pointer and returns. It is called by one other routine.

name: step_channel_event_stream
description: Runs one channel's event-stream step. When the channel counter reaches zero it reads the next command bytes from the channel's stream, sets a new duration and updates the stream pointer, then returns the channel's current value.

name: decode_stream_command_byte
description: Decodes one command byte from an event stream. Values in the upper range store a pointer into a table entry, the terminator sets an end flag, and values in the next range store a four-bit field. Other values do nothing.

name: advance_channel_note_timer
description: Advances a channel's note timer. A stored value with its top bit clear is returned directly. Otherwise it counts down a short timer and, at zero, reads the next stream byte to set a new length and offset.

name: initialise_channel_from_source
description: Stores a decimal-adjusted value and copies several fields from a source record into the channel record. It sets two flag bits in the channel status byte and records a handler pointer.

name: initialise_channel_record_fields
description: Copies several fields from a source record into the channel record, sets two flag bits, and stores a handler pointer, then returns its input register.

name: write_audio_channel_block
description: When a status bit is set it writes four channel fields into a block (an address, a length, a period and a volume), then clears a flag bit and sets a mode value when a mask matches. It calls a handler at the end.

name: update_audio_channel_hardware
description: When bit fourteen of the channel flags is set, it copies the volume, period, address and length fields into the channel's hardware registers and decrements a length counter. It then calls a handler, and when the channel mask is clear it also clears its flag and sets the DMA and interrupt enable bits.

name: step_and_clamp_counter
description: Adds a signed step to a byte counter. When the result goes negative or reaches a limit, it clamps the counter to the limit and sets a handler pointer.

name: step_counter_within_bounds
description: Adds a step to a byte counter. If the result leaves the range set by two bounds, it resets the counter to the bound that was passed and sets a handler pointer.

name: set_handler_when_zero
description: When a 16-bit field is zero, it sets the record's handler pointer to a fixed routine. Otherwise it does nothing.

name: step_and_reset_channel_block
description: Adds a step to a counter. When the result goes negative while a flag bit is clear, it clears that flag and sets a period and an address on the channel block.

name: clear_fixed_work_block
description: Zeroes a fixed work block of 1658 bytes starting at its fixed address, one byte at a time.

name: clear_flag_and_xor_copy
description: Clears one bit in a flag byte selected by the input value, then copies a table of words with an XOR applied while counting down a count from a table. The routine ends in a decoder halt, so the code after the loop is not reliable.

name: clear_flag_and_xor_copy
description: Clears one bit in a flag byte selected by the input value, then copies a table of words with an XOR applied while counting down a count from a table. The routine ends in a decoder halt, so the code after the loop is not reliable.

name: clear_flag_and_xor_copy
description: Clears one bit in a flag byte selected by the input value, then copies a table of words with an XOR applied while counting down a count from a table. The routine ends in a decoder halt, so the code after the loop is not reliable.

name: clear_flag_and_xor_copy
description: Clears one bit in a flag byte selected by the input value, then copies a table of words with an XOR applied while counting down a count from a table. The routine ends in a decoder halt, so the code after the loop is not reliable.
